A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Material relocated between the main text and appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, gradient and Hessian measurements, training curves, and test accuracies for RoBERTa, ViT, and ResNet18.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds normalization-placement experiments and nanoGPT training results on Shakespeare.

M1.justification: The analyzed optimizers, gradient-based and sign-based update rules, and training objectives remain unchanged. The added normalization variants are experimental controls, rather than changes to a proposed optimization method.

E1.justification: Appendix F.10 adds Shakespeare language modeling from scratch using nanoGPT, extending coverage beyond fine-tuning classification. The original nine NLP and vision datasets remain; normalization variants on existing datasets change experimental configurations.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same Adam, SGD, SignSGD, RMSProp, momentum variants, and scheduling comparisons. The new nanoGPT experiment uses Adam, SGD, and SignSGD, all already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The new normalization experiment controls the RoBERTa backbone, varies normalization placement and initialization, and trains scratch-initialized models for 1,000 iterations. The nanoGPT experiment introduces training from scratch with minimum and final training-loss summaries. Existing fine-tuning splits, budgets, and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix F.9 add a focused ablation testing normalization placement using No-LN, Pre-LN, and Post-LN RoBERTa on RTE and CB. This supplements v1's comparisons across different architectures. Existing scheduling, momentum, and attention analyses remain, including relocated material.

E5.justification: Figure 1 changes from individual batch observations to explicitly reported means for parameter blocks, reducing the displayed within-block variation. The stated one tuning seed, five training seeds, standard-deviation reporting, and interquartile training-curve bands remain unchanged; no increase in runs is reported.

E6.justification: New results include RTE scratch-model Gini coefficients of 0.867, 0.880, and 0.941 for No-LN, Pre-LN, and Post-LN, respectively. Shakespeare final training losses are 0.687 for Adam, 0.964 for SGD, and 0.820 for SignSGD (Tables 2, 12–14). Original training curves, test accuracies, and existing Gini-table values are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 6 and Appendix D revise the Post-LN Jacobian so normalization Jacobians multiply the complete residual sums; layer-normalization outer-product expressions also change. Appendix C.2 corrects the sign-sequence recurrence from a gradient-sequence iterate to a sign-sequence iterate. The main complexity bounds and relocated momentum proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Gradient heterogeneity, normalization placement, and appropriately scheduled SignSGD remain the central claims. Momentum's regulation of linear-head growth is no longer a headline contribution in the abstract, introduction, or conclusion, although its proposition and evidence remain in Appendix G.

C2.justification: v2 elaborates the multiplicative normalization mechanism, adds explicit fine-tuning and training-versus-test limitations, and interprets nanoGPT results as supporting broader applicability. It removes v1 Appendix G.2's qualification that factors beyond attention matrices also influence the gradient bounds.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds the shared-backbone control and 1,000-iteration preparation for the normalization ablation. It removes the explanation of median-loss model selection and dimension normalization for the retained linear-head plots. Core implementation settings and the code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a prior-study comparison table, discusses Pan and Li's directional sharpness, and adds references including Maes, Choi, and Schmidt. Takase's normalization reference is removed. The main research positioning remains; numerous publication and citation-format updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively reorganized and edited, particularly the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Momentum theory, its proof, and experimental discussion are consolidated into Appendix G from several main-text and appendix locations, shifting the paper's presentation toward gradient heterogeneity and normalization.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from two columns to one. Figures and panels are redistributed between the main text and appendices, Hessian scatter plots are redrawn as block summaries, and literature-comparison and experimental tables are added. The standalone linear-head plot disappears while its equivalent appendix result remains.

improvement.justification: The controlled normalization ablation and corrected Post-LN Jacobian strengthen the architectural explanation, while nanoGPT adds limited evidence beyond fine-tuning. These gains outweigh modest losses in documentation, including the removed attention-analysis qualification and linear-head measurement details. Sparse settings for the new language-model experiment limit the overall improvement.
